title: Base-changed edge maps carry the unit of a composite to the pullback
statement:
Let $f:Y\to X$, $\pi:Y'\to Y$ and $i:Z\to X$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $f'=f\circ\pi$, and $G$ an abelian sheaf on $Y_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Put $Y_Z=Y\times_XZ$ and $Y'_Z=Y'\times_XZ$ [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $i_Y:Y_Z\to Y$, $f_Z:Y_Z\to Z$, $i_{Y'}:Y'_Z\to Y'$, $f'_Z:Y'_Z\to Z$, and let $\pi_Z=\pi\times_X\mathrm{id}_Z:Y'_Z\to Y_Z$, so that $i_Y\pi_Z=\pi i_{Y'}$ and $f_Z\pi_Z=f'_Z$; regard the two squares $(f,f_Z,i,i_Y)$ and $(f',f'_Z,i,i_{Y'})$ as cartesian squares [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with $\theta$ built from the composition isomorphisms as in [lem-weil-pbc-edge-map-base-change]. For a cartesian square $\square=(h,h',i,i')$ with $h:W\to X$ and an abelian sheaf $E$ on $W_{\Et}$ write
$$\Phi^q_{\square,E}=e^q_{h',i'^{-1}E}\circ H^q(\Ex^0_{\square,E}):H^q(Z_{\Et},i^{-1}h_*E)\to H^q((W\times_XZ)_{\Et},i'^{-1}E),$$
with $\Ex^0$ the underived exchange morphism [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] and $e^q$ the edge map of [lem-weil-pbc-edge-map-base-change] (pullback map [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] followed by $H^q$ of the counit). Let $u:f_*G\to f'_*\pi^{-1}G$ be $f_*(\eta_{\pi,G}):f_*G\to f_*\pi_*\pi^{-1}G$ followed by the identification $f_*\pi_*=(f\pi)_*$ of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] ($\eta_\pi$ the unit of $\pi^{-1}\dashv\pi_*$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]), and let $\kappa:\pi_Z^{-1}i_Y^{-1}G\xrightarrow{\sim}i_{Y'}^{-1}\pi^{-1}G$ be the composition isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] for $i_Y\pi_Z=\pi i_{Y'}$, i.e. $\kappa=c_{\pi,i_{Y'},G}^{-1}\circ c_{i_Y,\pi_Z,G}$ through $(i_Y\pi_Z)^{-1}G=(\pi i_{Y'})^{-1}G$. Then for every $q\ge0$
$$\Phi^q_{(f',f'_Z,i,i_{Y'}),\pi^{-1}G}\circ H^q(i^{-1}u)=H^q(\kappa)\circ\pi_Z^*\circ\Phi^q_{(f,f_Z,i,i_Y),G}:\ H^q(Z_{\Et},i^{-1}f_*G)\to H^q((Y'_Z)_{\Et},i_{Y'}^{-1}\pi^{-1}G),$$
$H^q(\varphi)$ denoting the map induced by a morphism of sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial]. No finiteness is needed; the case $Z=X$, $i=\mathrm{id}$ is allowed. (Intended proof: [lem-weil-pbc-edge-map-base-change] for both squares reduces the claim to the case $i=\mathrm{id}$, where it follows from clauses 3 (naturality) and 4 (composition) of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] and the triangle identity $\varepsilon_{f'}\circ f'^{-1}(u)=\pi^{-1}(\varepsilon_f)$ composed with the identifications, up to the composition isomorphisms.)

proof.text: *Step 1 (notation and conventions).* Put $A=f_*G$ on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], $B=i^{-1}A$ on $Z_{\Et}$, $A'=f'_*\pi^{-1}G$. The squares of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] give the equalities of morphisms $f\circ i_Y=i\circ f_Z$, $f'\circ i_{Y'}=i\circ f'_Z$, $f_Z\circ\pi_Z=f'_Z$, $i_Y\circ\pi_Z=\pi\circ i_{Y'}$ ($\pi_Z=\pi\times_X\mathrm{id}_Z$ is the morphism with these two compositions), $f\circ\pi=f'$; so all composites $Y'_Z\to X$ below are one morphism $k=i f'_Z=i f_Z\pi_Z=f i_Y\pi_Z=f\pi i_{Y'}=f' i_{Y'}$ and have one inverse image $k^{-1}$. Units and counits of $s^{-1}\dashv s_*$ are $\eta_s,\varepsilon_s$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]; $c_{s,t}:t^{-1}s^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}(st)^{-1}$ and $d_{s,t}:(st)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}s_*t_*$ are the isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (1), (2), so $u=d^{-1}_{f,\pi,\pi^{-1}G}\circ f_*(\eta_{\pi,G})$ and $\kappa=c^{-1}_{\pi,i_{Y'},G}\circ c_{i_Y,\pi_Z,G}$ (natural in $G$, as the $c$ are). For a cartesian square $\square=(h,h',i,i')$ as in the statement, $\theta_\square=c^{-1}_{h,i'}\circ c_{i,h'}$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], [lem-weil-pbc-edge-map-base-change], and $\Ex^0_{\square,E}=h'_*(\varphi_{\square,E})\circ\eta_{h',i^{-1}h_*E}$ is the adjoint under $h'^{-1}\dashv h'_*$ of $\varphi_{\square,E}=i'^{-1}(\varepsilon_{h,E})\circ c^{-1}_{h,i',h_*E}\circ c_{i,h',h_*E}:h'^{-1}i^{-1}h_*E\to i'^{-1}E$ [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange]. Cohomology groups and maps are read as in step 1 of [lem-weil-pbc-edge-map-base-change]: a K-injective resolution [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions] of every sheaf occurring is fixed, each $H^q(T_{\Et},-)$ is computed from it, each pullback map $s^*$ [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] is followed by the identification $H^q(\mathrm{id})$ with the fixed resolution of the target (independent of the auxiliary resolution by clause 1 of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial]), and $H^q(\psi)$ for a morphism of sheaves $\psi$ is as in the preamble of that lemma. Then $H^q(\psi'\circ\psi)=H^q(\psi')\circ H^q(\psi)$ and $H^q(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$ (a composite of lifts is a lift of the composite; $H^q(-)$ does not depend on the lift: step 1(b) of the proof of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial], written out as step 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-edge-map-base-change]), so $H^q$ of an isomorphism is bijective with inverse $H^q(\psi^{-1})$. The identity to be proved does not depend on the choices, since other choices change every map by the identifications $H^q(\mathrm{id})$ on source and target.

proof.text: *Step 2 ($\Phi$ through one pullback map).* For a square $\square=(h,h',i,i')$ and $E$ as in the statement, $\Phi^q_{\square,E}=H^q(\varphi_{\square,E})\circ h'^*$ as maps $H^q(Z_{\Et},i^{-1}h_*E)\to H^q((W\times_XZ)_{\Et},i'^{-1}E)$. Indeed, by [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity] for $h'^{-1}\dashv h'_*$, $\psi=\Ex^0_{\square,E}=h'_*(\varphi_{\square,E})\circ\eta_{h'}$ gives $\varepsilon_{h',i'^{-1}E}\circ h'^{-1}(\Ex^0_{\square,E})=\varphi_{\square,E}$ (step 3 of [lem-weil-pbc-edge-map-base-change]). By definition $\Phi^q_{\square,E}=H^q(\varepsilon_{h',i'^{-1}E})\circ h'^*\circ H^q(\Ex^0_{\square,E})$; clause 3 (naturality) of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] for $h'$ and $\Ex^0_{\square,E}$ gives $h'^*\circ H^q(\Ex^0)=H^q(h'^{-1}\Ex^0)\circ h'^*$, and by step 1 $H^q(\varepsilon_{h'})\circ H^q(h'^{-1}\Ex^0)=H^q(\varepsilon_{h'}\circ h'^{-1}\Ex^0)=H^q(\varphi_{\square,E})$. Write $\varphi_1=\varphi_{(f,f_Z,i,i_Y),G}:f_Z^{-1}B\to i_Y^{-1}G$ and $\varphi_2=\varphi_{(f',f'_Z,i,i_{Y'}),\pi^{-1}G}:f'^{-1}_Zi^{-1}A'\to i_{Y'}^{-1}\pi^{-1}G$.

proof.text:
*Step 3 (reduction to an identity of sheaf morphisms).* Left side: by step 2 and clause 3 of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] for $f'_Z$ and the morphism $i^{-1}u:B\to i^{-1}A'$ of $\Ab(Z_{\Et})$, $\Phi^q_2\circ H^q(i^{-1}u)=H^q(\varphi_2)\circ f'^*_Z\circ H^q(i^{-1}u)=H^q(\varphi_2\circ f'^{-1}_Zi^{-1}(u))\circ f'^*_Z$ (step 1). Right side: by step 2 and clause 3 for $\pi_Z$ and $\varphi_1$, $H^q(\kappa)\circ\pi_Z^*\circ\Phi^q_1=H^q(\kappa)\circ H^q(\pi_Z^{-1}\varphi_1)\circ\pi_Z^*\circ f_Z^*$; by clause 4 (composition) for $u=f_Z$, $v=\pi_Z$ and the sheaf $B$, $f'^*_Z=(f_Z\pi_Z)^*=H^q(c_{f_Z,\pi_Z,B})\circ\pi_Z^*\circ f_Z^*$, so $\pi_Z^*\circ f_Z^*=H^q(c^{-1}_{f_Z,\pi_Z,B})\circ f'^*_Z$ (step 1). Hence the right side is $H^q(\kappa_G\circ\pi_Z^{-1}(\varphi_1)\circ c^{-1}_{f_Z,\pi_Z,B})\circ f'^*_Z$. So the lemma follows from the identity of morphisms $f'^{-1}_ZB\to i_{Y'}^{-1}\pi^{-1}G$ in $\Ab((Y'_Z)_{\Et})$
$$(\star)\qquad \varphi_2\circ f'^{-1}_Zi^{-1}(u)=\kappa_G\circ\pi_Z^{-1}(\varphi_1)\circ c^{-1}_{f_Z,\pi_Z,B},$$
proved in steps 4–7.

proof.text: *Step 4 (the counit of $f'$ on $u$).* Claim: $\varepsilon_{f',\pi^{-1}G}\circ f'^{-1}(u)=\pi^{-1}(\varepsilon_{f,G})\circ c^{-1}_{f,\pi,A}:f'^{-1}A\to\pi^{-1}G$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity] for $f'^{-1}\dashv f'_*$ it suffices that $u=f'_*(\rho)\circ\eta_{f',A}$ for $\rho=\pi^{-1}(\varepsilon_{f,G})\circ c^{-1}_{f,\pi,A}$. The unit equation [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (2) for $(f,\pi)$ at $A$ gives $\eta_{f',A}=d^{-1}_{f,\pi,f'^{-1}A}\circ f_*\pi_*(c_{f,\pi,A})\circ f_*(\eta_{\pi,f^{-1}A})\circ\eta_{f,A}$. Naturality of $d_{f,\pi}$ gives $f'_*(\rho)\circ d^{-1}_{f,\pi}=d^{-1}_{f,\pi}\circ f_*\pi_*(\rho)$, hence $f'_*(\rho)\circ\eta_{f',A}=d^{-1}_{f,\pi,\pi^{-1}G}\circ f_*\bigl(\pi_*\pi^{-1}(\varepsilon_{f,G})\circ\eta_{\pi,f^{-1}A}\bigr)\circ\eta_{f,A}$. Naturality of $\eta_\pi$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] for $\varepsilon_{f,G}:f^{-1}A\to G$ gives $\pi_*\pi^{-1}(\varepsilon_{f,G})\circ\eta_{\pi,f^{-1}A}=\eta_{\pi,G}\circ\varepsilon_{f,G}$, and the triangle identity $f_*(\varepsilon_{f,G})\circ\eta_{f,f_*G}=\mathrm{id}_{f_*G}$ [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity] then gives $f'_*(\rho)\circ\eta_{f',A}=d^{-1}_{f,\pi,\pi^{-1}G}\circ f_*(\eta_{\pi,G})=u$.

proof.text: *Step 5 (the left side of $(\star)$).* $\varphi_2=i_{Y'}^{-1}(\varepsilon_{f',\pi^{-1}G})\circ c^{-1}_{f',i_{Y'},A'}\circ c_{i,f'_Z,A'}$ (step 1). Naturality of $c_{i,f'_Z}$ and of $c_{f',i_{Y'}}$ [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (2) for $u:A\to A'$: $c_{i,f'_Z,A'}\circ f'^{-1}_Zi^{-1}(u)=k^{-1}(u)\circ c_{i,f'_Z,A}$ and $c^{-1}_{f',i_{Y'},A'}\circ k^{-1}(u)=i_{Y'}^{-1}f'^{-1}(u)\circ c^{-1}_{f',i_{Y'},A}$. With step 4 (and functoriality of $i_{Y'}^{-1}$): $\varphi_2\circ f'^{-1}_Zi^{-1}(u)=i_{Y'}^{-1}\pi^{-1}(\varepsilon_{f,G})\circ i_{Y'}^{-1}(c^{-1}_{f,\pi,A})\circ c^{-1}_{f',i_{Y'},A}\circ c_{i,f'_Z,A}$.

proof.text: *Step 6 (the right side of $(\star)$).* $\pi_Z^{-1}(\varphi_1)=\pi_Z^{-1}i_Y^{-1}(\varepsilon_{f,G})\circ\pi_Z^{-1}(c^{-1}_{f,i_Y,A})\circ\pi_Z^{-1}(c_{i,f_Z,A})$ (step 1, $\pi_Z^{-1}$ a functor), and naturality of $\kappa$ (step 1) for $\varepsilon_{f,G}:f^{-1}A\to G$ gives $\kappa_G\circ\pi_Z^{-1}i_Y^{-1}(\varepsilon_{f,G})=i_{Y'}^{-1}\pi^{-1}(\varepsilon_{f,G})\circ\kappa_{f^{-1}A}$. Hence the right side of $(\star)$ is $i_{Y'}^{-1}\pi^{-1}(\varepsilon_{f,G})\circ c^{-1}_{\pi,i_{Y'},f^{-1}A}\circ c_{i_Y,\pi_Z,f^{-1}A}\circ\pi_Z^{-1}(c^{-1}_{f,i_Y,A})\circ\pi_Z^{-1}(c_{i,f_Z,A})\circ c^{-1}_{f_Z,\pi_Z,B}$.

proof.text: *Step 7 (coherence of the composition isomorphisms).* By steps 5 and 6 it suffices that the isomorphisms $\Lambda=i_{Y'}^{-1}(c^{-1}_{f,\pi,A})\circ c^{-1}_{f',i_{Y'},A}\circ c_{i,f'_Z,A}$ and $P=c^{-1}_{\pi,i_{Y'},f^{-1}A}\circ c_{i_Y,\pi_Z,f^{-1}A}\circ\pi_Z^{-1}(c^{-1}_{f,i_Y,A})\circ\pi_Z^{-1}(c_{i,f_Z,A})\circ c^{-1}_{f_Z,\pi_Z,B}$, both $f'^{-1}_Zi^{-1}A\to i_{Y'}^{-1}\pi^{-1}f^{-1}A$, are equal. Use the associativity of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition] (1): for composable $s,t,r$, $c_{s,tr}\circ(c_{t,r}s^{-1})=c_{st,r}\circ(r^{-1}c_{s,t})$ $(\mathrm{As})$. Compose both with the isomorphism $T=c_{f',i_{Y'},A}\circ i_{Y'}^{-1}(c_{f,\pi,A}):i_{Y'}^{-1}\pi^{-1}f^{-1}A\to k^{-1}A$; then $T\circ\Lambda=c_{i,f'_Z,A}$. By $(\mathrm{As})$ for $(f,\pi,i_{Y'})$ (with $f\pi=f'$), $T=c_{f,\pi i_{Y'},A}\circ c_{\pi,i_{Y'},f^{-1}A}$, so $T\circ P=c_{f,i_Y\pi_Z,A}\circ c_{i_Y,\pi_Z,f^{-1}A}\circ\pi_Z^{-1}(c^{-1}_{f,i_Y,A})\circ\pi_Z^{-1}(c_{i,f_Z,A})\circ c^{-1}_{f_Z,\pi_Z,B}$ ($\pi i_{Y'}=i_Y\pi_Z$). By $(\mathrm{As})$ for $(f,i_Y,\pi_Z)$, $c_{f,i_Y\pi_Z,A}\circ c_{i_Y,\pi_Z,f^{-1}A}=c_{fi_Y,\pi_Z,A}\circ\pi_Z^{-1}(c_{f,i_Y,A})$, so $T\circ P=c_{if_Z,\pi_Z,A}\circ\pi_Z^{-1}(c_{i,f_Z,A})\circ c^{-1}_{f_Z,\pi_Z,i^{-1}A}$ ($fi_Y=if_Z$). By $(\mathrm{As})$ for $(i,f_Z,\pi_Z)$, $c_{if_Z,\pi_Z,A}\circ\pi_Z^{-1}(c_{i,f_Z,A})=c_{i,f_Z\pi_Z,A}\circ c_{f_Z,\pi_Z,i^{-1}A}$, so $T\circ P=c_{i,f'_Z,A}=T\circ\Lambda$ ($f_Z\pi_Z=f'_Z$). As $T$ is an isomorphism, $P=\Lambda$.

proof.text: *Step 8 (conclusion).* By steps 5, 6 and 7 both sides of $(\star)$ equal $i_{Y'}^{-1}\pi^{-1}(\varepsilon_{f,G})\circ\Lambda$, so $(\star)$ holds, and by step 3 $\Phi^q_{(f',f'_Z,i,i_{Y'}),\pi^{-1}G}\circ H^q(i^{-1}u)=H^q(\kappa)\circ\pi_Z^*\circ\Phi^q_{(f,f_Z,i,i_Y),G}$ for every $q\ge0$. No finiteness of $f$ or $\pi$ was used, and $Z=X$, $i=\mathrm{id}$ is covered.
